title: Psalms Chapter 113 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 113 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 113 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 113.

questions.question: Who are specifically called to praise the LORD in Psalms 113:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Servants of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:1 states, 'Praise, O ye servants of the LORD, praise the name of the LORD,' directly calling the servants to praise.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:2, how long should the name of the LORD be blessed?
options: From this time forth and for evermore
Until the end of the year
questions.correctAnswer: From this time forth and for evermore
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:2 says, 'Blessed be the name of the LORD from this time forth and for evermore,' indicating continuous blessing.

questions.question: What is the LORD's name to be praised from, according to Psalms 113:3?
options: From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same
From the east to the west
questions.correctAnswer: From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:3 explicitly states, 'From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD'S name is to be praised.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 113:1 commands that only kings should praise the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse calls specifically 'servants of the LORD' to praise, not kings exclusively, as stated in Psalms 113:1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:4, where is the LORD placed in relation to nations and heavens?
options: High above all nations and his glory above the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: High above all nations and his glory above the heavens
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:4 states, 'The LORD is high above all nations, and his glory above the heavens,' showing His exalted position.

questions.question: Who, according to Psalms 113:5, is like unto the LORD our God?
questions.correctAnswer: No one
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:5 asks rhetorically, 'Who is like unto the LORD our God?' implying no one is like Him.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 113:6 says the LORD humbles Himself to look at things only in heaven.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:6 states the LORD humbles Himself to behold things in both heaven and earth, not heaven only.

questions.question: Which action does the LORD perform according to Psalms 113:7?
options: He raises the poor out of the dust
He makes the sun stand still
questions.correctAnswer: He raises the poor out of the dust
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:7 says, 'He raiseth up the poor out of the dust,' showing His care for the needy.

questions.question: In Psalms 113:8, what position does the LORD set the needy to?
questions.correctAnswer: With princes of his people
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:8 states, 'That he may set him with princes, even with the princes of his people,' indicating elevation to honor.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 113:9 describes the LORD making the barren woman a joyful mother of children.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:9 clearly states, 'He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children.'

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of praise instructions in Psalms 113:1 to 3?
options: Praise the LORD; Bless the name of the LORD forever; Praise from sunrise to sunset
Bless the name of the LORD forever; Praise from sunrise to sunset; Praise the LORD
Praise from sunrise to sunset; Praise the LORD; Bless the name of the LORD forever
Bless the name of the LORD forever; Praise the LORD; Praise from sunrise to sunset
questions.correctAnswer: Praise the LORD; Bless the name of the LORD forever; Praise from sunrise to sunset
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:1 commands to praise the LORD, 113:2 blesses His name forever, and 113:3 instructs praise from sunrise to sunset in this order.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:3, until when should the LORD’s name be praised?
options: Until the going down of the sun
questions.correctAnswer: Until the going down of the sun
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:3 clearly states the LORD's name is to be praised from sunrise until sunset.

questions.question: Who is instructed to praise the name of the LORD in Psalms 113:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Servants of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:1 explicitly addresses 'servants of the LORD' to praise His name.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 113:2 mentions blessing the name of the LORD only for today.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:2 states blessing the name of the LORD from this time forth and forevermore, not just for today.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:4, the LORD's glory is above what?
questions.correctAnswer: The heavens
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:4 says the LORD's glory is above the heavens, indicating His supreme majesty.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 113 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 113 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:4, where is the LORD described as being exalted?
options: Above all nations and above the heavens
On the earth among the people
questions.correctAnswer: Above all nations and above the heavens
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:4 states that the LORD is high above all nations and his glory above the heavens, emphasizing His supreme exaltation.

questions.question: What does Psalms 113:5 express about the uniqueness of the LORD our God?
options: He dwelleth on high and is unmatched
He is like the other gods of the nations
He is far from the humble
questions.correctAnswer: He dwelleth on high and is unmatched
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:5 asks who is like unto the LORD our God, emphasizing His unique dwelling on high and incomparable nature.

questions.question: How does Psalms 113:6 describe God's attitude towards the things in heaven and earth?
options: He humbles Himself to behold them
questions.correctAnswer: He humbles Himself to behold them
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:6 explains that the LORD humbles Himself to look upon the things in heaven and earth, showing His care and attention.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about humility based on Psalms 113:5-6?
options: God is exalted yet humbles Himself to care for creation
God only cares for the heavens, not the earth
God demands worship but does not engage with creation
questions.correctAnswer: God is exalted yet humbles Himself to care for creation
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 together show that while God dwells on high and is exalted, He humbles Himself to behold and care for all things in heaven and earth.

questions.question: A believer struggles to understand how God can be both mighty and caring. How does Psalms 113:4-6 address this?
options: God is exalted above all but humbles Himself to observe and care for creation
God is only mighty and does not care for individuals
God is weak and cannot intervene
questions.correctAnswer: God is exalted above all but humbles Himself to observe and care for creation
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:4-6 reveal God's supreme exaltation alongside His humility in caring for the things in heaven and earth, encouraging trust in His power and compassion.

questions.question: What does Psalms 113:7 teach about God’s care for the needy?
options: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the dunghill
He only cares for the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the dunghill
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:7 shows God's active care by raising the poor and needy from lowly conditions, highlighting His compassion.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:8, what is the purpose of God lifting the needy?
options: To set them with princes, even with the princes of His people
questions.correctAnswer: To set them with princes, even with the princes of His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:8 explains that God raises the needy to a position of honor, placing them among princes, showing His ability to elevate the lowly.

questions.question: How does Psalms 113:9 illustrate God's power in transforming lives?
options: He makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children
He leaves the barren woman without hope
questions.correctAnswer: He makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:9 shows God's transformative power by enabling the barren woman to bear children joyfully, symbolizing hope and blessing.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 113:1 commands servants of the LORD to praise His name.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:1 clearly instructs servants of the LORD to praise His name, emphasizing worship and praise as a duty.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 113:3, the LORD’s name is to be praised only during the day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:3 states the LORD’s name is to be praised from the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, implying continuous praise throughout daylight hours.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 113:2 blesses the name of the LORD from now and forevermore.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:2 declares that the name of the LORD is blessed from this time forth and forevermore, showing eternal praise.

questions.question: What does Psalms 113:6 say about God's engagement with creation?
options: He humbles Himself to behold the things in heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: He humbles Himself to behold the things in heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:6 highlights God's humility as He observes all things in heaven and earth, showing His intimate involvement.

questions.question: How does Psalms 113:7-8 demonstrate God's justice and mercy?
options: He raises the poor and needy to positions of honor
He leaves the poor in their place
questions.correctAnswer: He raises the poor and needy to positions of honor
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 show God’s mercy by lifting the poor and needy from lowly places and setting them with princes, indicating His justice and grace.

questions.question: What promise is implied if one praises the LORD as urged in Psalms 113:1-2, based on the entire chapter’s context?
options: God will exalt the lowly and bless the needy
questions.correctAnswer: God will exalt the lowly and bless the needy
questions.explanation: The chapter connects praise to God’s character of lifting the poor and blessing the barren, implying that praising Him aligns believers with His blessing (verses 1-2, 7-9).

questions.question: What does Psalms 113:4-6 teach about trusting God during difficult times?
options: Though God is exalted, He humbles Himself to care for us, so we can trust His attentiveness
God is too high to notice our troubles
We must rely only on ourselves
questions.correctAnswer: Though God is exalted, He humbles Himself to care for us, so we can trust His attentiveness
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize God's exaltation alongside His humility and care, encouraging believers to trust Him even in hardship (verses 4-6).

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 113 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 113.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:7, what does the LORD do for the poor?
options: He raises them up out of the dust
He gives them wealth and riches
questions.correctAnswer: He raises them up out of the dust
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:7 states that the LORD 'raiseth up the poor out of the dust,' showing His action of elevating the humble and needy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the LORD lifting the needy out of the dunghill as stated in Psalms 113:8?
options: That he may set him with princes
That he may give him land
That he may protect him from enemies
That he may make him a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: That he may set him with princes
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:8 explains that God lifts the needy so that he may be set 'with princes, even with the princes of his people,' indicating elevation to honor and status.

questions.question: In Psalms 113:9, what transformation does the LORD bring about in the barren woman?
options: Makes her a joyful mother of children
Leads her to the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: Makes her a joyful mother of children
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:9 states that the LORD 'maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children,' showing a miraculous change in her condition.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God lifting the humble in Psalms 113:7-8?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 2:8
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:8 contains a similar theme: 'He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth the needy out of the dunghill,' paralleling Psalms 113:7-8.

questions.question: The phrase 'from the dust' in Psalms 113:7 is an example of what literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: The term 'dust' metaphorically represents lowliness or poverty, illustrating the LORD's power to raise the humble, as stated in Psalms 113:7.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 113:9 implies that the LORD only works miracles for barren women in ancient Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: While Psalms 113:9 mentions the barren woman, the LORD's power is universal and not limited to barren women in Israel; this verse highlights His ability to bring joy and transformation.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is often translated as 'barren' in Psalms 113:9, and what does it imply in the original context?
questions.correctAnswer: Ishshah rahah, meaning barren woman
questions.explanation: The Hebrew phrase 'Ishshah rahah' literally means 'barren woman,' emphasizing the condition of childlessness addressed in Psalms 113:9.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God exalting the humble, as seen in Psalms 113:7-8?
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 1:52
questions.explanation: Luke 1:52 echoes this theme with the Magnificat: 'He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree,' paralleling Psalms 113:7-8.

questions.question: What cultural significance does the LORD's act of setting the needy 'with princes' in Psalms 113:8 have in the ancient Near East?
options: It signifies social elevation and honor
It means becoming a military leader
It implies exile to foreign lands
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies social elevation and honor
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, being seated with princes indicated high social status and honor, which Psalms 113:8 uses to illustrate God's power to exalt the lowly.

questions.question: Which theme from Psalms 113:7-9 is fulfilled in the New Testament story of the Virgin Mary?
options: God making the barren woman joyful with children
God giving wealth to the poor
God calling prophets to the nations
questions.correctAnswer: God making the barren woman joyful with children
questions.explanation: Mary, considered barren before conceiving Jesus by the Holy Spirit, fulfills the theme in Psalms 113:9 of the LORD making the barren woman joyful with children.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 113:1-3 precedes the final third of the chapter and focuses on praising the LORD's name from sunrise to sunset.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:1-3 indeed calls for praise of the LORD from 'the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same,' setting the worship context before the final verses about God's actions.

questions.question: In Psalms 113:6, what does it mean that God 'humbleth himself to behold the things that are in heaven, and in the earth'?
options: God stoops to notice both heaven and earth
God is limited to earth only
God is hidden from the world
God ignores the needs of people
questions.correctAnswer: God stoops to notice both heaven and earth
questions.explanation: The verse shows God's condescension or humility in observing all creation, emphasizing His care for both the heavenly and earthly realms.

questions.question: Which literary structure best describes Psalms 113:1-9 as a whole?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Psalms 113 uses an inclusio structure, opening and closing with calls to praise the LORD, framing the middle content about His exaltation of the humble.

questions.question: What does the exaltation of the poor and needy in Psalms 113:7-8 foreshadow about God's kingdom?
options: The reversal of social status in God's kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The reversal of social status in God's kingdom
questions.explanation: The lifting of the lowly anticipates the kingdom values where the humble are exalted, contrasting worldly social orders.

questions.question: How does the theme of God making the barren woman joyful in Psalms 113:9 connect to earlier Scripture promises?
options: It fulfills God's promise of numerous descendants to Abraham
It relates to the covenant with Noah
It recalls the Law given to Moses
It references the Exodus from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills God's promise of numerous descendants to Abraham
questions.explanation: God's transformation of the barren woman reflects the fulfillment of His promise to Abraham of many descendants, as in Genesis 17:16-19.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 113 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 113 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:1, who are specifically called to praise the name of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Servants of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:1 explicitly calls 'ye servants of the LORD' to praise the name of the LORD, emphasizing the role of God’s servants in worship.

questions.question: What eternal blessing is pronounced on the name of the LORD as stated in Psalms 113:2?
options: Blessed from this time forth and for evermore
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed from this time forth and for evermore
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:2 blesses the name of the LORD 'from this time forth and for evermore,' showing the eternal nature of God's praise.

questions.question: What does Psalms 113:3 teach about the scope of praising the LORD's name?
options: From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof
Only by the priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof
questions.explanation: Verse 3 stresses continuous praise of God’s name throughout the day, illustrating the comprehensive and perpetual worship due to God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily highlighted by Psalms 113:4 stating 'The LORD is high above all nations, and his glory above the heavens'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's transcendence
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:4 reveals God's transcendence as He is described as being 'high above all nations' and His glory above the heavens, emphasizing His supreme majesty.

questions.question: Psalms 113:5 asks, 'Who is like unto the LORD our God, who dwelleth on high?' What theological truth does this question affirm?
options: The uniqueness and sovereignty of God
questions.correctAnswer: The uniqueness and sovereignty of God
questions.explanation: This verse emphasizes God's incomparable nature and sovereign position 'dwelleth on high,' affirming His uniqueness among all beings.

questions.question: What does Psalms 113:6 reveal about God's relationship to creation?
options: He humbles Himself to behold the things in heaven and earth
He dwells only in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: He humbles Himself to behold the things in heaven and earth
questions.explanation: The verse shows God's humility and immanence in relation to His creation, indicating His attentive care despite His exalted position.

questions.question: According to Psalms 113:7, what action does God take regarding the poor and needy?
options: He raises the poor out of the dust and lifts the needy out of the dunghill
He leaves them in their lowly state
questions.correctAnswer: He raises the poor out of the dust and lifts the needy out of the dunghill
questions.explanation: This verse highlights God's justice and mercy in uplifting the lowly and needy, reflecting His concern for the marginalized.

questions.question: What is the ultimate purpose for God raising the needy 'that he may set him with princes' as stated in Psalms 113:8?
options: To exalt them to positions of honor among His people
questions.correctAnswer: To exalt them to positions of honor among His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 113:8 teaches that God exalts the lowly to be honored alongside princes, demonstrating His sovereign grace and reversal of worldly status.

questions.question: How does Psalms 113:9 illustrate God's power over human barrenness and joy?
options: He makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children
He punishes barrenness as a curse
He only blesses kings with children
questions.correctAnswer: He makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children
questions.explanation: This verse shows God's power to transform barrenness into fruitfulness and joy, symbolizing His life-giving and covenantal blessings.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Psalms 113:4 and Psalms 113:6 convey about God's nature?
options: God is both transcendent above all and immanently involved with creation
God only interacts with the heavens
God is limited to earthly realms
questions.correctAnswer: God is both transcendent above all and immanently involved with creation
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows God's transcendence 'above all nations,' while verse 6 reveals His humility and involvement with creation, together expressing the complex unity of God's nature.

questions.question: How do Psalms 113:7 and Psalms 113:8 together reflect the doctrine of God's justice and mercy?
options: God uplifts the poor and needy to positions of honor, demonstrating mercy and justice
God punishes the poor by keeping them lowly
God judges all nations equally without mercy
God's justice is limited to the righteous only
questions.correctAnswer: God uplifts the poor and needy to positions of honor, demonstrating mercy and justice
questions.explanation: Verse 7 describes God raising the poor, and verse 8 explains the purpose to exalt them among princes, highlighting His just and merciful character.

questions.question: Integrating Psalms 113:2 and Psalms 113:9, what doctrine about God's enduring blessing and provision is taught?
options: God's blessing is eternal and includes restoring joy and fruitfulness
God's blessings are temporary and conditional
God only blesses the righteous kings
questions.correctAnswer: God's blessing is eternal and includes restoring joy and fruitfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 2 blesses God's name eternally, while verse 9 shows God giving joy to the barren, together affirming God's everlasting and restorative blessings.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is distant and unconcerned with human suffering. What does Psalms 113:6-8 actually teach about God's engagement with humanity?
options: God humbles Himself to see and raise the lowly out of their suffering
God is unconcerned and indifferent to human affairs
God condemns the poor to remain in misery
God only interacts with rulers and the powerful
questions.correctAnswer: God humbles Himself to see and raise the lowly out of their suffering
questions.explanation: Verses 6-8 reveal God's humility in observing both heaven and earth and His active role in uplifting the poor and needy, directly countering claims of divine indifference.

questions.question: What theological insight about God's sovereignty and human dignity is drawn by combining Psalms 113:5 and Psalms 113:8?
options: God's sovereign exaltation includes uplifting the lowly to share in His people’s honor
God only values the high and mighty
God is indifferent to human status
Human dignity is independent of God's will
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign exaltation includes uplifting the lowly to share in His people’s honor
questions.explanation: Verse 5 proclaims God's high dwelling and uniqueness; verse 8 shows His power to exalt the needy among princes, showing sovereign grace elevates human dignity.

questions.question: How does Psalms 113:3 contribute to the biblical theology of worship in the redemptive narrative?
options: It teaches continuous praise of God from sunrise to sunset, reflecting ongoing worship in creation
It restricts worship to temple rituals only
It limits praise to special feast days
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches continuous praise of God from sunrise to sunset, reflecting ongoing worship in creation
questions.explanation: This verse mandates praise throughout the day, aligning with the biblical theme of creation and humanity continuously glorifying God amid redemptive history.
